subject: biology
topicDisplay: Theme D · Cells (Division, Gene Expression, Water Potential)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Mitosis produces daughter nuclei that are:
options: Genetically identical to the parent nucleus
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid nuclei for growth, repair and asexual reproduction.

questions.q: Meiosis is described as a reduction division because it:
options: Halves the chromosome number, producing haploid cells
Keeps the chromosome number the same
questions.explain: Meiosis produces gametes with half the chromosome number, restored to diploid at fertilisation.

questions.q: Genetic variation in gametes is increased during meiosis by:
questions.explain: Crossing over and the random orientation of homologous pairs (independent assortment) shuffle alleles, plus random fertilisation adds variation.

questions.q: The correct order of the main phases of mitosis is:
questions.explain: Chromosomes condense (prophase), align (metaphase), separate (anaphase) and reform nuclei (telophase).

questions.q: Cancer is best described as a disease resulting from:
questions.explain: Mutations in genes controlling the cell cycle can cause unchecked division, forming tumours.

questions.q: Gene expression can be regulated so that:
options: Different cell types make different proteins from the same genome
Cells lose genes they do not use
questions.explain: Regulation of transcription and translation allows differentiation without changing the DNA sequence.

questions.q: Epigenetic changes such as DNA methylation typically:
options: Switch genes off without changing the DNA base sequence
questions.explain: Methylation and histone modification alter gene activity and can be influenced by the environment.

questions.q: Proteins that bind to DNA and control whether a gene is transcribed are:
questions.explain: Transcription factors bind regulatory regions (e.g. promoters) to switch transcription on or off.

questions.q: The observation that identical twins can develop different disease risks over time is partly explained by:
questions.explain: Environmental factors can cause epigenetic differences that alter gene expression despite an identical genome.

questions.q: Water moves by osmosis from a region of:
options: Higher water potential to lower water potential
questions.explain: Water potential falls as solute concentration rises; water moves down its water potential gradient.

questions.q: A plant cell placed in a hypotonic (dilute) solution will:
options: Take in water and become turgid
Burst like a red blood cell
questions.explain: Water enters by osmosis; the cell wall prevents bursting, so the cell becomes firm (turgid).

questions.q: When a plant cell is placed in a strongly hypertonic solution, the membrane pulls away from the wall in a process called:
questions.explain: Water leaves the cell by osmosis, the cytoplasm shrinks and the membrane detaches from the cell wall.

questions.q: An animal cell has no cell wall, so in a hypotonic solution it may:
questions.explain: Without a wall to resist pressure, water uptake can cause an animal cell to lyse.

questions.q: In which type of division would you expect crossing over to occur?
questions.explain: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes occurs in prophase I of meiosis, not in mitosis.

questions.q: A human body (somatic) cell is diploid, meaning it contains:
questions.explain: Diploid cells (46 chromosomes in humans) carry two copies of each chromosome; gametes are haploid.

questions.q: The environment can affect the phenotype by:
questions.explain: Phenotype results from interaction of genotype and environment, partly through effects on gene expression.

questions.q: An isotonic solution is one in which:
options: There is no net movement of water into or out of the cell
questions.explain: Isotonic solutions have equal water potential to the cell, so water movement is balanced.

questions.q: A checkpoint failure that allows a cell with damaged DNA to divide can contribute to:
questions.explain: Cell-cycle checkpoints normally halt division of damaged cells; their failure can lead to cancer.

questions.q: Water potential is highest (closest to zero) in:
questions.explain: Pure water has a water potential of zero; adding solute makes it more negative.

questions.q: Regions of DNA to which RNA polymerase and transcription factors bind to start transcription are called:
questions.explain: Promoters are regulatory sequences that control the initiation of transcription of a gene.
